intent: A discovery told as a gap: the dish in a London hospital in 1928, then thirteen years in which the mould was useless because nobody could make enough; a real wartime photo of the flasks rises out of Britain, a FOUND / MADE split carries the two dates, and the 1945 Nobel closes it — a body quiz about the drug that made surgery survivable.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country DISCOVERED penicillin?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Britain. In 1928 a London doctor came back from holiday and found mould killing bacteria in a dish.

lines.direction: ease back over the British Isles; the US flag-ball thinks on 'America' with a factory sticker; a pill sticker on 'Germany'; a pointer sticker on 'here' as Britain pulses
lines.text: America mass-produced it in the war, and Germany had other drugs. But the mould was spotted here.

lines.direction: tighten on the Midlands; an hourglass sticker on 'enough' as the real 1943 production photo rises out of Britain with a flash; a police-officer sticker on 'policeman'; an empty-battery sticker on 'out' as Britain pulses softly; the photo leaves at the end
lines.text: Nobody could make enough for thirteen years. The first patient, a policeman, improved, then the supply ran out.

lines.direction: ease back over southern England; the Oxford pin on 'Oxford' and the FOUND / MADE split of the two dates; the split leaves for the 1945 NOBEL card on 'three' with a medal sticker; the British flag-ball grins; a no-entry sticker on 'fourth' as Britain pulses; the pins leave at the end
lines.text: An Oxford team made it a drug in 1940. Three men shared the 1945 Nobel Prize, and a fourth was left out.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A dish of mould. Follow us.
